question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=e{x}^{2-5{x}^{2}}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(e{x}^{2-5{x}^{2}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡e+\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2-5{x}^{2}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =1+(2-5{x}^{2})\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1+(2-5{x}^{2})\operatorname{ln}⁡x) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =0+(2-5{x}^{2})^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+(2-5{x}^{2})\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(-10x)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡x+(2-5{x}^{2})\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =-10x\operatorname{ln}⁡x+\frac{2-5{x}^{2}}{x} \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =-10x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-5x+\frac{2}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(-10x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-5x+\frac{2}{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=e{x}^{2-5{x}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =e{x}^{2-5{x}^{2}}\cdot (-10x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-5x+\frac{2}{x}) \\  & =e{x}^{1-5{x}^{2}}\cdot x(-10x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-5x+\frac{2}{x}) \\  & =e{x}^{1-5{x}^{2}}\cdot (-10{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-5{x}^{2}+2)\end{aligned}
$$
